A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same UniCSG work. Their complete text, equations, tables, figures and Appendices A–D support reliable comparison despite extensive reformatting and appendix renumbering.

before.justification: V1 reports original benchmark results, component ablations, seen/unseen-style evaluations, qualitative outputs and a user study with 30 evaluators.

after.justification: V2 retains the work's original benchmark results, ablations, generalization evaluations, qualitative outputs and user-study outcomes.

M1.justification: The backbone, conditioning corruption, semantic losses, frequency supervision and pixel-space reward objective remain unchanged. Sections 3 and 3.3 clarify shared text/reference conditioning and reward learning across both stages without changing the procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions retain CSG-Dataset training, CSG-Bench and OmniConsistency-Bench evaluation, text-guided and reference-guided tasks, and the same content domains and seen/unseen style coverage.

E2.justification: Corresponding benchmark tables retain the same eight external baselines and Qwen-Image-Edit base model. Comparator membership also remains unchanged in the user study and Nano-banana failure-case comparisons.

E3.justification: Both report 40,000 training tuples, 12,000/8,000 training steps, the same A100 setup and hyperparameters, 1,922 benchmark content images and six evaluation metrics. The user study still uses 30 evaluators and 48 cases.

E4.justification: The Stage 1, Stage 2 and reward ablations, seen/unseen-style evaluation, and text-distortion and hand-gesture failure analyses are retained. Appendix D redisplays the same supporting examples under revised figure numbers.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed or repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests for the comparisons. Statistical reporting practices remain unchanged.

E6.justification: All numerical results in Tables 1–6 and v1 Tables 7–8 versus v2 Tables B.1–B.2 are identical, and the qualitative outputs are retained. Section 4.2.2 adds specific qualitative observations about hairstyle, semantic identity, object-count and background-layout preservation.

T1.justification: Equations 1–13 and the frequency-decomposition and corruption-schedule formulations in Appendix C remain mathematically unchanged. No formal assumptions, theorems, proofs or derivations are added or removed.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution list and conclusion retain the same claims concerning semantic disentanglement, frequency-aware reconstruction, perceptual alignment and improved content-preserving stylization.

C2.justification: V2 emphasizes style-content tradeoffs and limitations of automatic metrics. Section 5 replaces the difficulty-tier discussion with category-level versus image-level stylization, qualifies unseen-style generalization, and removes the comparative speed-superiority assertion while retaining the reported 4-second/10-second latencies.

D1.justification: V2 adds a front-page code/data repository address and correspondence contact; the PDFs alone do not verify repository availability. Implementation settings remain unchanged, but Appendix A removes citations identifying de-stylization sources and the aesthetic-assessment model.

R1.justification: V2 adds Chefer et al.'s Self-supervised flow matching for scalable multi-modal synthesis in Section 3.1. References to ArtiMuse, the original ViT paper, OmniStyle2 and the LPIPS paper disappear. The principal related-work discussion remains essentially unchanged.

P1.justification: V2 adds localized method and results explanations, rewrites part of Section 5, and introduces numbered experimental and discussion subheadings. The main section sequence, appendices and most prose remain intact.

P2.justification: V2 adopts a substantially different branded layout with wider text, green headings and a boxed abstract. Figures are enlarged and relocated throughout; main metric tables gain grouped style/content headers. Existing displays are retained with revised appendix numbering.

improvement.justification: V2 modestly improves clarity through explicit method explanations, clearer metric grouping and a code/data pointer. Section 5 better qualifies unseen-style degradation and removes a comparative speed claim unsupported by a reported timing comparison. These gains are partly offset by lost appendix source attributions; the method and experimental evidence remain unchanged.
